body.name: Adaptive singularity-to-oracle handle
body.construction: Under \(\texttt{ass:iid-triangular-sampling}\), \(\texttt{ass:primitive-moment-envelope}\), \(\texttt{ass:primitive-covariance}\), and \(\texttt{ass:regular-primitive-map}\), let \(m_n=\lfloor n^{2/3}\rfloor\), use \(m_n\) observations as a pilot subsample, and use the independent remaining subsample of size \(N_n=n-m_n\) for inference.  On the inference subsample choose \(\varepsilon_{N_n}\to0\) with \(\sqrt{N_n}\,\varepsilon_{N_n}\to\infty\).  Define \(\mathsf H_n\) by a deterministic diagonal calibration over compact inner sieves of the finitely many strict regular cells.  The pilot selects numerical-delta inference only if a shrinking closed neighborhood of its primitive mean and covariance is contained in one inner sieve with positive denominator, ratio-order, branch-selection, primal-slack, dual-slack, reduced-cost, and endpoint-variance margins.  On that event, \(\mathsf H_n\) is the slab determined by the outer lower and upper \(q\)-support endpoints of the inference-subsample numerical-delta intervals; otherwise \(\mathsf H_n\) is the inference-subsample undivided inversion set.  The inner sieves and continuity moduli define an existence and calibrated-sieve construction; no globally implementable modulus or ball-containment algorithm is asserted.
